title: Supreme Court asks Election Commission to check complaint of fake voter-deletion forms in Delhi's Mustafabad
dek: The court told the Commission and Delhi's poll officer to verify a Congress leader's allegation that false Form 7s were filed to strike genuine voters off the roll during the SIR.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The Supreme Court on Thursday told the Election Commission and Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer to verify a Congress leader's complaint that false applications were filed to delete genuine voters from the electoral roll of Delhi's Mustafabad constituency during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR), and to take remedial steps if the complaint was found to be true.

A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana disposed of the petition filed by Ali Mehdi (W.P.(C) 1493/2026) without expressing any opinion on the merits, because he had already complained to the police, the Election Commission and the Chief Electoral Officer, according to reports of the hearing. The authorities are to act "strictly in accordance with law", the bench said.

## What the petition said

Form 7 is the application used to object to a name on the voter list or to ask for it to be deleted, for example because the voter has died or moved away. The petition alleged that Form 7s had been filed in the names of booth-level agents, the representatives political parties appoint to work with election officials at each polling booth, and that most of those agents denied having signed them. Voters marked for deletion as dead or shifted were alive and living at their addresses, it said. Counsel for the petitioner told the court that 36 of the 37 Form 7s filed were false, and said the police had refused to register a first information report on his complaint. The court did not test these figures.

Justice Bagchi said the Election Commission does not control booth-level agents, who act for parties, but added: "If a booth-level agent makes a fraudulent application, the Election Commission can blacklist him." On the refusal to register an FIR, he told the petitioner: "Approach the Magistrate."

## The wider fight over the SIR

The SIR is the Election Commission's door-to-door re-verification of voter lists, which it is carrying out in phases across states. Opposition parties have accused it of being used to strike off eligible voters, particularly among minorities and migrants; the Commission says it is cleaning the rolls of dead, shifted and duplicate entries and that no eligible voter will be left out.

The Mustafabad petition relied on an earlier order of the same bench. On 30 October, hearing a challenge to the SIR in Uttar Pradesh, the court directed the Commission to examine allegations of bulk Form 7 filings, take corrective steps and file a compliance report. In that case the Commission's counsel told the court that the bulk Form 7s "were false and we have not acted" on them, according to reports.

On Wednesday the Commission extended the date for publishing final rolls under the SIR in Jharkhand, Maharashtra, Delhi, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Nagaland and Haryana from 30 November to 22 December, to allow more time to verify absent, shifted, dead and duplicate voters, according to reports. Uttar Pradesh published its draft roll this week, listing 13.58 crore voters, and the Samajwadi Party has alleged a plan to add fake voters there, which the BJP denies.

## What happens next

The Chief Electoral Officer of Delhi must now verify the Mustafabad complaint. The petitioner can approach a magistrate to seek an FIR. Other challenges to the SIR in several states remain pending before the Supreme Court.
